**3B.5 Research Note**

Bottom line: I found strong evidence that Hasina used emergency-style controls in 2024 as tools of coercion and information suppression, not as narrowly lawful public-safety measures. I did not find credible 2024 evidence of a disciplined, rights-respecting emergency framework; the closest pro-state material is defensive border management on Rohingya flows, which is only a weak and indirect fit.

- [Bangladesh army enforces curfew as student-led protests spiral](https://theprint.in/world/bangladesh-army-enforces-curfew-as-student-led-protests-spiral/2182818/) — Reuters, July 20, 2024. Claim: Reuters reported a nationwide curfew and internet/text shutdown as the government escalated against protesters; this is direct evidence of emergency-like controls being used to intimidate opponents and suppress scrutiny. IDs: `3B.5`, `3B.1`, `3B.2`, `2B.4`, `2B.6`
- [Bangladesh PM Hasina blames opposition for violence, curfew to remain](https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/bangladesh-pm-hasina-blames-opposition-for-violence-curfew-to-remain-3528153) — Reuters, July 22, 2024. Claim: Hasina kept the curfew in place and blamed political opponents for the violence, which looks like coercive administrative control and collective blame rather than narrow lawful use. IDs: `3B.5`, `3B.3`, `3B.1`, `2B.6`, `2B.7`
- [Bangladesh’s crackdown on protesters left more than 170 dead, U.N. says](https://bangladesh.un.org/en/275065-bangladesh-t%C3%BCrk-decries-government-crackdown-urges-respect-international-human-rights) — United Nations / OHCHR, July 26, 2024. Claim: The UN said more than 170 people had been killed and warned that internet shutdowns increase impunity; this strongly supports the view that the government used emergency controls as a coercive instrument, not a lawful, narrowly tailored one. IDs: `3B.5`, `3B.1`, `3B.2`, `2B.4`, `2B.9`
- [Exclusive: Bangladesh army refused to suppress protest, sealing Hasina’s fate](https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/exclusivebangladesh-army-refused-to-suppress-protest-sealing-hasinas-fate-3558302) — Reuters, August 6, 2024. Claim: Reuters reported the army would not fire on civilians to enforce Hasina’s curfew; that implies the coercive apparatus was being pushed toward lethal enforcement, not bounded legal necessity. IDs: `3B.5`, `3B.1`, `3B.2`, `2B.4`, `2B.9`
- [Former Bangladesh PM Hasina demands probe into July "killings and vandalism"](https://theprint.in/world/former-bangladesh-pm-hasina-demands-probe-into-july-killings-and-vandalism/2222256/) — Reuters, August 13, 2024. Claim: After fleeing, Hasina called for an investigation into the killings and vandalism; this is the only weak accountability signal I found, but it is post-hoc and does not show that emergency powers were used lawfully while she controlled them. IDs: `3B.5`, `2B.9`
- [Bangladesh will not let in any more Rohingya refugees: minister](https://theprint.in/world/bangladesh-will-not-let-in-any-more-rohingya-refugees-minister/1958020/) — Reuters, February 7, 2024. Claim: Bangladesh framed refusing additional Rohingya as a security necessity; this is the closest 2024 defensive-administration evidence I found, but it is indirect, voiced by a minister, and not evidence of narrowly lawful emergency powers by Hasina herself. IDs: `3B.5`, `2B.3`
- [Bangladesh ramps up border vigilance as thousands of Rohingya flee Myanmar](https://theprint.in/world/bangladesh-ramps-up-border-vigilance-as-thousands-of-rohingya-flee-myanmar/2262488/) — Reuters, September 11, 2024. Claim: Bangladesh tightened border vigilance amid renewed violence in Myanmar and refugee flows; this is a defensive administrative control in response to external instability, but it does not show rights-respecting emergency governance inside Bangladesh. IDs: `3B.5`, `2B.3`

**Search Gap**
- I did not find reliable 2024 evidence that Hasina used emergency powers, security laws, surveillance, or administrative controls in a narrowly tailored and lawful way.
- I also did not find evidence of strong judicial review, independent oversight, or complaint mechanisms constraining those controls in 2024.
- The available record points much more clearly to coercion, shutdowns, and impunity than to lawful, limited emergency governance.
